chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him):'

"O Son of the Messenger of Allah! Verily, the people relate that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah created Adam in His Image.'" He (peace be upon him) replied: "May Allah kill them! They have certainly removed the first part of the tradition. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by two men who were cursing each other. He (peace be upon him) heard one of them say to the other: 'May Allah make your face and the face of the one who resembles you ugly!' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O servant of Allah! Do not say this to your brother, for verily Allah, the Mighty and High, created Adam in His Image.'

key_terms.أَوَّلَ الْحَدِيثِ: The first part of the tradition
key_terms.قُبْحَ اللَّهُ وَجْهَكَ: May Allah make your face ugly

ai.seo_question: What is the full context of the hadith 'Allah created Adam in His Image'?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to clarify the doctrine of *tashbih* (resemblance) by distinguishing between the physical form and the divine essence, noting that the Prophet’s reference to 'His Image' specifically pertains to the face (*wajh*) as a locus of divine beauty rather than implying corporeal anthropomorphism. This context is crucial for Shia theological debates against the Mu'tazila and Ahl al-Sunnah regarding whether the 'face' mentioned in the Quran is an attribute or the essence itself, affirming that humans bear a created reflection of the Divine. The correction of the truncated narration underscores the precision required in transmitting hadith to avoid theological misinterpretation.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 11. Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja`far al-Hamadani (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of His father, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ma`bad, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Khalid that I said to al-Rida (sw):

“O Son of the Messenger of Allah! Verily, the people relate that the Messenger of Allah (sw) said: “Verily, Allah created Adam (sw) in His Image.”” He (AS) replied: May Allah kill them! They have certainly removed the first part of the tradition. The Messenger of Allah (sw) passed by two men who were cursing each other. He (sw) heard one of them say to the other: “May Allah make your face and the one who resembles you ugly!” He (sw) said: “O servant of Allah! Do not say this to your brother for, verily Allah, the Mighty and High, created Adam (AS) in His Image.”
